title: Model catalog
description: The maintainers' rating of tuples, shipped with the package. One row per thing that can actually be launched; only rated tuples enter automatic selection.

schemaVersion.description: Version of the catalog format. A newer one blocks the load rather than being read half-understood.

tuples.description: Rated tuples. An id occurs once: the resolver's last tie-break is the id, and a duplicate would make the pick order-dependent.

timestamp.description: Exactly what Date#toISOString prints: date-time alone would admit offsets.

rating.description: Maintainer rating on the 1-5 scale. Integers: half a point is a judgement the source cannot support.

quotaCost.description: Spend against the subscription. Inverted when scored: a smaller spend contributes more.

price.description: USD per 1M tokens, or null when the billing mode makes it meaningless or the price is not published.

id.description: Stable id. It survives a model rename, and it is the resolver's final tie-break.

harness.description: Harness the tuple runs on. Checked against the host's declaredTools() at load.

model.description: Model id as the harness binary names it. For a harness that carries effort inside the id, the full id including that suffix.

effort.description: Effort level passed to the driver, from that driver's EFFORT_LEVELS; null for a harness that takes no separate effort flag.

roles.description: Roles this tuple may be picked for. A reviewer-only or worker-only tuple is normal.

roleRatings.description: Per-role overrides of the ratings above. Only the named keys are replaced.

billing.description: subscription — the spend is against a plan; payg — it is money per token, and the tuple stays out of automatic selection without --allow-payg.

priority.description: Canonical priority, used only as a tie-break. Lower comes first.

source.description: Where the rating came from. A rating with no source is a hypothesis and stays out of the catalog.

evidence.description: What a later maintainer checks the rating against. A bare string is the v1 form and still holds. The object form is what ADR-004 asks for once ratings come from published results: it carries the citation per rating, so `validate` can refuse a rated row that has none.

citation.description: One published figure behind one rating. ADR-004 asks for the benchmark or price source, the figure, the size of the field it was banded against, the source URL and the date seen; the agent harness is named because a Terminal-bench figure without it is not a figure, and `provenance` says whether the page cited was the one actually opened.

basis.description: The benchmark or the price source, named as the source names it.

version.description: Version of the benchmark. Two versions of one benchmark are two benchmarks: the same model moves tens of points between them.

agentHarness.description: Agent harness the figure was measured under, or a sentence saying the page does not state one. A benchmark that scores the model and the harness together produces a different number per harness.

provenance.description: Whether the cited page is the one that was opened, and whether it is primary or secondary.

fieldSize.description: How many rated models the band was cut from. A rank band over a small field is a rank band over a small field, and the reader is told the size.

date.description: The date the source was seen, as YYYY-MM-DD.

text.description: The prose a later maintainer reads first.

sources.description: One entry per rating that rests on a published figure.

interpolatedFrom.description: Tuple id of the base row this one was interpolated from. The base row holds the citations and the ladder shares its assessedAt, so a ladder goes stale together.

hypothesis.description: Ratings with no published figure for this exact model. ADR-004 refuses to invent one: the row says so, and the band stays the maintainers' reasoning.

tuples.source: schema example — not a rating of any real model
tuples.evidence: placeholder row; the shipped catalog is PB-13
